issues: No attempt to get around the measurement: no file or network access, no pasted answers, and no use of test labels. Ranking happens only among the test-fold predictions, which is fine because the harness scores each fold separately with Spearman.

No bug that makes the result meaningless. Mapping the averaged ranks back to the y range, then applying expm1, keeps the order, so Spearman is unchanged. The second check `np.all(y_train >= 0)` runs on y values that are already log-transformed. It is still true whenever the first check was true, so expm1 is applied correctly. The unused variables `sorted_y` and `sorted_indices` are dead code and harmless.
Code quality: the diff has a lot of rambling, self-contradicting comments, a check that tests the same condition twice, and dead variables. This conflicts with the 'simpler is better' rule.

The candidate is worse than the incumbent: 0.5534 vs 0.5155, a difference of +0.0379. Using noise sd 0.0070 for each single run, the sd of the difference is 0.0099, so z ≈ -3.83. That matches the harness value of -3.817 within rounding. Reject is the right decision.
Both sides have only one run, so the comparison is noisy. Still, a gap of about 3.8 sd is a clear worsening.
